title: Review: Chemistry — The periodic table
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for KS3 Science (chemistry) (status of the source: authored-reviewed-reverified-2026-10-08). Terms and clues: C6#c27 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C6#c12 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C6#c21 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; C6.6#xt1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C6#q08, C6#q11, C6#q15, C6#q21, C6#q10, C6#q14, C6#q17, C6#q20, C6#x02 (written for the game), C6#q12, C6#q18, C6#q19. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Base
items.clue: A substance that neutralises an acid.

items.label: Group
items.clue: A vertical column of the periodic table.

items.label: Non-metal
items.clue: Typically dull, brittle and a poor conductor.

items.label: Acid rain
items.clue: Precipitation with a low pH, caused by gases such as sulfur dioxide

questions.stem: In the periodic table, what is a period?

options.text: A row of elements going across the table
A column of elements down the table
A family of elements that react alike
A list of elements in order of reactivity

questions.explanation: Yes. A period is a horizontal row. Properties change across a period, from metals on the left to non-metals on the right.

questions.stem: Potassium is below sodium in Group 1. Bromine is below chlorine in Group 7. Compared with the element above it, how reactive is each?

options.text: Potassium more; bromine more
Potassium less; bromine less
Potassium less; bromine more
Potassium more; bromine less

questions.explanation: Yes. Going down Group 1 the metals get more reactive, so potassium beats sodium. Going down Group 7 the halogens get less reactive, so bromine is less reactive than chlorine.

questions.stem: Which property do all metals have?

options.text: They are attracted to a magnet
They are solid at room temperature
They can conduct electricity
They have high melting points

questions.explanation: Yes. Every metal conducts electricity. Most metals are solid and hard, but not all, and only a few, such as iron, are attracted to a magnet.

questions.stem: Copper oxide powder is stirred with water and filtered. The filtered water has pH 7. What is copper oxide?

options.text: A neutral oxide, as the water is pH 7
A base, as it can neutralise acids
An acidic oxide, like any oxide
An alkali, as it is a metal oxide

questions.explanation: Yes. Copper oxide neutralises acids, for example making copper sulfate with sulfuric acid, so it is a base. It does not dissolve, so the water stays at pH 7.

questions.stem: What does the staircase line on the periodic table separate?

options.text: Metal elements from non-metals
Reactive elements from unreactive ones
Solid elements from gaseous ones
Shiny elements from dull elements

questions.explanation: Yes. Metals are to the left of the staircase line and non-metals to its right. Most elements are metals.

questions.stem: Sodium burns in chlorine. Xenon is in Group 0, below krypton. Predict what happens when sodium is heated in xenon.

options.text: It burns, as xenon is a gas like chlorine
It reacts, as xenon is low in its group
Unknown until someone has tested it
No reaction, as xenon is a noble gas

questions.explanation: Yes. The Group 0 elements, the noble gases, hardly react at all, so sodium will not burn in xenon as it does in chlorine.

questions.stem: Sodium is soft enough to cut with a knife and melts at 98 °C. Is sodium a metal, and why?

options.text: Yes: each sodium atom is soft and shiny
No: metals are hard and difficult to melt
Yes: it is one of the alkali metals
No: a magnet does not attract it

questions.explanation: Yes. Sodium is in Group 1, the alkali metals, and it is shiny when cut and conducts electricity. Not every metal is hard with a high melting point.

questions.stem: Element X burns in oxygen. Its oxide dissolves in water, making a solution of pH 3. What is X most likely to be?

options.text: A metal, since metal oxides are acidic
A metal, as non-metals do not burn
Either, as all oxides are acidic
A non-metal, as its oxide is acidic

questions.explanation: Yes. pH 3 is acidic, and non-metal oxides, such as sulfur dioxide, make acidic solutions. X is most likely a non-metal such as sulfur.

questions.stem: Element Z is in Group 2, on the left of the periodic table. Which properties is Z most likely to have?

options.text: Shiny when cut, and a good conductor of electricity
Dull and brittle, and a poor conductor of electricity
A colourless gas that does not conduct electricity
Magnetic, as every metal is attracted to a magnet

questions.explanation: Elements on the left of the periodic table are metals: shiny, and good conductors of electricity.

questions.stem: Rubidium is just below potassium in Group 1. How will rubidium react with water, compared with potassium?

options.text: Less vigorously, as the top one reacts most
Just as vigorously, as it is in one group
More vigorously, as it is lower in the group
Unknown, as only a test can show this

questions.explanation: Yes. Reactivity increases going down Group 1, so rubidium reacts even more violently than potassium, making hydrogen and an alkaline solution.

questions.stem: Element W is dull and grey. It conducts electricity, a magnet does not attract it, and it can be hammered flat. What is W, and how can you tell?

options.text: A metal, as only metals conduct electricity
A non-metal, as it is dull, not shiny
A metal, as it is malleable and conducts
A non-metal, as magnets do not attract it

questions.explanation: Yes. Being malleable (it can be hammered flat without breaking) and conducting electricity are typical of metals. A metal's surface often looks dull after it has reacted with the air.

questions.stem: Sodium oxide and calcium oxide are metal oxides that dissolve in water. What do they form?

options.text: An alkaline solution
An acidic solution
Just a neutral solution
Hydrogen and an alkali

questions.explanation: Yes. These metal oxides are bases, and because they dissolve they make alkaline solutions, with a pH above 7.
